question: What is the primary focus of quality improvement in nursing?

options.A: Punishing staff who make clinical mistakes
options.B: Structured methods to evaluate and upgrade services
options.C: Increasing the cost of hospital admissions
options.D: Reducing the total number of working nurses

explanation: Quality improvement uses systematic frameworks to monitor and better healthcare delivery for patients. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why do healthcare facilities rely on structured quality improvement methods?

options.A: To ensure safer patient care and reduce errors
options.B: To comply with international tourism policies
options.C: To make daily nursing tasks much longer to complete
options.D: To replace doctors with administrative personnel

explanation: Systematic evaluation helps identify workflow gaps, thereby protecting patients from preventable medical errors. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h1)

question: What do the letters PDSA stand for in healthcare management?
explanation: PDSA stands for Plan, Do, Study, and Act, which is a four-stage problem-solving model. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why is the PDSA cycle used for small-scale tests?

options.A: To hide clinical failures from senior hospital management
options.B: To safely test interventions before hospital-wide rollout
options.C: To increase the workload of junior student nurses
options.D: To make nursing documentation completely unnecessary

explanation: Small-scale testing allows teams to see if an intervention works without risking full-scale disruption. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the first activity performed during the Plan phase of a PDSA cycle?

options.A: Setting a clear objective and defining goals
options.B: Throwing away all old hospital equipment
options.C: Discharging every patient currently on the ward
options.D: Punishing staff members for past clinical mistakes

explanation: Every successful project begins by clearly stating what the team intends to accomplish during planning. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h3)

question: A nurse manager wants to reduce patient wait times in the clinic. What belongs in the Plan phase?

options.A: Defining the objective and planning data collection methods
options.B: Purchasing expensive computers for the entire hospital
options.C: Firing the reception staff for poor time management
options.D: Guessing the final results without collecting any data

explanation: The Plan phase focuses on setting goals, making predictions, and figuring out how to measure success. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h3)

question: What happens during the Do phase of the PDSA cycle?

options.A: The planned intervention is tested on a small scale
options.B: The management team writes a final textbook chapter
options.C: The entire project is permanently abandoned
options.D: The nurses take a mandatory extended vacation

explanation: The Do phase involves putting the planned change into action to see how it operates in real life. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why is recording unexpected problems important during the Do phase?

options.A: It helps the team understand practical barriers in real-time
options.B: It gives nurses a reason to complain to the director
options.C: It replaces the need to ever study the collected data
options.D: It guarantees that funding will be doubled immediately

explanation: Documenting surprises helps explain why outcomes might differ from predictions during the evaluation step. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the main activity during the Study phase of the PDSA cycle?

options.A: Buying new medical supplies for the emergency unit
options.B: Transferring all patients to a different hospital
options.C: Comparing actual results with the original predictions
options.D: Writing a brand new curriculum for nursing schools

explanation: The Study phase is where data is analyzed to see if the intervention produced the expected outcome. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is a major risk of skipping the Study phase?

options.A: The hospital will save a large amount of money
options.B: Doctors will take over all nursing administrative tasks
options.C: Patients will recover much faster than expected
options.D: Ineffective or harmful changes might be adopted blindly

explanation: Without studying results, teams cannot tell if a change genuinely helped or caused hidden harm. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which three choices summarize the decision options in the Act phase?
explanation: Teams use the findings to either adopt the change, tweak it through adaptation, or abandon it entirely. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h6)

question: A new handwashing routine failed to reduce infection rates during a PDSA test. What should the team do in the Act phase?

options.A: Punish the ward nurses for failing the project
options.B: Adopt the routine as official hospital policy immediately
options.C: Hide the infection data from the medical director
options.D: Abandon the routine and test a different strategy

explanation: When an intervention does not work, abandoning it prevents wasting resources on an ineffective practice. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which local challenge is commonly encountered when running healthcare projects in Nigeria?

options.A: Zero patient admissions across all public facilities
options.B: An excess of unused hospital beds in every ward
options.C: Erratic power supply and resource scarcity
options.D: Too many working computers for every single nurse

explanation: Nigerian healthcare facilities often manage operations under tight resource constraints and infrastructure challenges. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why is involving frontline staff crucial for PDSA success in Nigerian clinical units?

options.A: It ensures staff ownership and sustainability of the project
options.B: It eliminates the need to ever collect patient data
options.C: It guarantees automatic promotion for all junior nurses
options.D: It prevents doctors from working night shifts on the ward

explanation: When frontline workers help design and test changes, they remain committed to making them work long-term. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h7)
